Subject: Pilot Onramp Playbook: seedboard draft + compact acceptance path

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled together a compact "seedboard" MAP and a short acceptance cadence that is designed for a 21-day pilot (we also call it a compact 21d path). The goal is to get a lightweight, testable integration in front of your product team and measure the three success criteria you mentioned (response quality, per-request latency, and inference cost per 1k tokens).

What I attached:
- Nimble_MAP_seedboard_v0.1.gdoc (seed MAP: milestones, owners, risks, acceptance test cases)
- Compact-21d-Acceptance-Slate.pptx (slides: week-by-week checklist + kickstart agenda)
- nimble_mvp_requirements.xlsx (tech readiness checklist we discussed — data access, sample volumes, API credentials)

Key asks:
1) Confirm primary stakeholders (eng, product, security) who will be part of the week0 sync.
2) Review the acceptance criteria table on page 2 of the gdoc and comment with any missing metrics.
3) Can we lock a 60-minute kickstart workshop on Mon/Tue next week? I put proposed times in the linked calendar (below).

Proposed next steps after your confirmation:
- Week0: Kickstart workshop (alignment, access, instrumenting eval harness)
- Week1: Core integration + smoke tests
- Week2: Performance tuning + evals vs. baseline
- Week3: Acceptance review and decision meeting

Links / invites: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NlmbLE-seedboard-v01 (view/comment)
Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=nimble-workshop-20260921
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/2987

Attachments: [Attachment: Nimble_MAP_seedboard_v0.1.gdoc] [Attachment: Compact-21d-Acceptance-Slate.pptx] [Attachment: nimble_mvp_requirements.xlsx]

Appreciate a quick read — I can iterate the MAP in real-time during the workshop if you'd like.

Best,

Thanks Tessa — this looks encouraging. Quick notes after a skim: 

- High level: the 21d approach makes sense to our PM and infra leads.
- Success criteria: can you add a pass/fail threshold for "response quality" (we typically use a human-rated correctness score > 0.8 on a 100-sample set)?
- Data access: our security team will need a short SOW + data handling summary before they approve access. Could you send a light SOW template or pointer to a compliance packet?

We added a couple things inline in the gdoc (comments). Also attaching a very short internal note that lists our initial sample data sources.

Attachments: [Attachment: nimble_internal_samples.docx]

Proposed times for kickoff: Mon 21 Sep 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue 22 Sep 08:30-09:30 PT — either works for Rajiv and me.

Subject: Fwd: Pilot Onramp Playbook: seedboard draft + compact acceptance path — internal notes

Tessa / team — forwarding Emily's notes. I pulled a quick internal pass with suggested edits we should make before the kickoff. TL;DR: add explicit thresholds, a pared-down SLO table, and an "approval gate" for security that maps to a single deliverable (SOW + data handling bulleted note).

Edits I recommend we push into the gdoc now:
- Response quality: add a column for "sample size" and "pass threshold" (default: 100 samples / 0.80 human score).
- Latency: specify p95 < 350ms (with warm cache) as the target for pilot acceptance.
- Cost: upper-bound on cost per 1k tokens for the pilot and an estimate section that ties to batching/cache recommendations.
- Security: include a one-page summary (2-3 bullets) that security can sign off on without a full audit — attach as a separate doc.

Owners (proposed):
- Tessa: stakeholder coordination + acceptance decision meeting
- Marissa: success criteria, acceptance test harness (will coordinate eval script)
- Ben: infra/throughput tuning and quantization guidance
- Jonas: billing estimate and slot planning for dedicated capacity (if needed)

I also drafted a short SOW template (attached) that the security team can use for initial approval.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_sow_template_for_pilot.docx]

If you want, I'll push these changes into the shared gdoc and flag them as \"redwood: proposed\" comments.

—Marissa
